newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Foreign investment in Romania on the rise.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Romania on the rise.

text.p: Romania's main foreign investment promoter said on Friday total direct foreign investments rose by $120.25 million in the first quarter this year, or 35 percent up from the same period of 1996.
"The rise was due mainly to capital increases at existing joint ventures," a Romanian Development Agency (ARD) official told Reuters.
The Netherlands topped foreign investors in terms of the size of the capital invested, followed by South Korea and Germany, while Italy had the largest number of joint-ventures.

Total direct foreign investment in Romania since it shed communism in 1989 stood at $2.318 billion early in April, an amount local analysts say Romania now needs every year to go deeper with reforms towards a market economy.
In a bid to lure foreign investment, the ARD has worked out amendments to legislation aimed at simplifying investment procedures and granting more incentives.

The new facilities, to benefit companies with a capital of minimum $10 million, include tax breaks, extension of customs duties holidays and free acquisition of land and production spaces. Under the present rules, companies must invest a minimum $50 million to benefit from such facilities.

The centrist government coalition, which ousted leftists in last November's elections, has pledged to seek increased foreign investment. Parliament last month adopted a law granting foreigners the right to own land in Romania.
